text: Read with the earlier promise in mind, the two passages stand closer than they seem. The writer recalls that Isaac is the child of the covenant, the one through whom the nations are to be blessed; and then that promise becomes a test. Much depends on a single word. Abraham answers with _hineni_, "here I am," three times; the word means something different each time, and each time it costs him more, so that to be present is for him to lose. He speaks it to God, to Isaac, and last to the angel.
